title: Refuse a missing or empty principles file at the kernel

completion.statement: state.py now refuses an empty principles file exactly as it refuses a missing one: the source-path check moved into require_source_file (shared by init and repair), which refuses a missing path, a zero-byte file and a whitespace-only file with a nonzero result naming the offending path (state: principles file missing|empty: <path>, exit 2) and never substitutes a built-in default. Five new PrinciplesPathGuardTests cover the missing, zero-byte, whitespace-only, direct-initialize and repair-consistency cases; all five failed pre-fix (empty file accepted with exit 0; missing message lacked the path). The rest of init's behavior is unchanged (56 test_state cases pass).
evidence: python3 -m unittest tests.test_state -v (56 tests OK; the 5 new guard tests failed pre-fix with exit 0 acceptance)

manual $TMPDIR run: populated -> exit 0; missing -> exit 2 'state: principles file missing: nope.md'; zero-byte -> exit 2 'state: principles file empty: empty.md' (file still 0 bytes after); whitespace-only -> exit 2 'state: principles file empty: ws.md'; refused programs created no run state
python3 -m compileall -q scripts skills tests; uvx --from ruff==0.17.0 ruff check .; python3 scripts/validate.py; python3 scripts/scan_public.py; python3 scripts/check_links.py (all clean)
